answer: An agent economy can price every trade by graph distance: fees rise with the shortest path from the identity to trusted seed agents in the trade graph, like a toll that grows the farther you stand from the ivory gates of the honest core. Each identity keeps its trading bond in a vault, and a fake sitting far from real counterparties pays a steep toll on every deal, while one honest agent near the center trades for a whisper of a fee. A sybil farmer would need to buy real trade edges for a thousand fakes, and even a zephyr of fake volume cannot fake closeness to real traders.
